item.title: Temporal Correlations Reshape Causal Resources in Qubit Hamiltonian Recognition: Exact Two-Query Strategy Comparison and a Uniform Critical Crossover
item.description: We investigate binary recognition of an unknown qubit Hamiltonian using two queries of its evolution, with unknown evolution angles that are either independently resampled or shared with tunable temporal correlation. For a symmetric pair of nonorthogonal qubit Hamiltonians, we compare parallel (PAR), sequential (SEQ), and general (GEN) quantum strategies. An exact symmetry reduction expresses the sequential optimization through a three-dimensional correlation elliptope. A general-strategy dual certificate establishes the equality between optimal general and sequential strategies within the studied model. We analyze the operational advantage generated by temporal correlations and establish distinct weak-correlation scaling regimes separated by a critical angle of 45 degrees. This revised and extended version (v1.2) adds a uniform double-scaling critical crossover theorem, including an explicit positive crossover function and consolidated mathematical proofs. The result characterizes a previously unresolved critical transition within the specified quantum Hamiltonian recognition model. The complete mathematical derivations are provided in the accompanying supplementary material (Sections S1–S19). This work is conducted within standard quantum information theory and does not claim physics beyond quantum mechanics. Version: 1.2 Resource type: Publication — Preprint Author: Youfu Wang Affiliation: Independent Researcher, OCN Research

item.title: QEM-8 II: A Hadamard-Tetrahedral-Spinor Framework for Eight-Outcome Qubit Geometry, Coarse-Graining, and History-Sensitive Tests
item.description: This preprint develops a mathematically explicit QEM-8 framework for a single qubit. It separates eight-state Bloch geometry, spinor sign double covers, and quaternionic operation history; derives the three-bit cube and parity-tetrahedral SIC structure; connects V4, H4 tomography, SU(2)/Q8 spinor lifts, and an eight-outcome cube POVM at the eta=1/sqrt(3) joint-measurability boundary; decomposes eight-outcome statistics into Walsh modes 1+3+3+1; and defines a rigorous 8->6->8' projection through a six-outcome Pauli representation. The residual Delta=p-p' lies in the four-dimensional high-order Walsh sector. Standard projective history effects (Gate 1A) are explicitly separated from a stronger, falsifiable history-residual hypothesis (Gate 1B). No experimental violation of standard quantum mechanics is claimed.

item.title: Measurement Aliasing and Pauli-Correlator Identifiability for Local Unitary Rotations of a Maximally Entangled Qubit Pair
item.description: We consider a restricted two-qubit model in which an unknown local unitary acts on one subsystem of a maximally entangled qubit pair and only local Pauli-product correlations are measured. We show that the three same-axis correlators XX, YY, and ZZ determine the magnitudes of the four components of the associated unit quaternion but, at generic interior points, leave an eightfold ambiguity in the underlying local rotation. We express this ambiguity as a sign fiber isomorphic to F2^3. The six cross-axis Pauli correlators separate into three rank-two sign-character subspaces. This structure yields a complete classification of the fifteen possible pairs of cross-axis correlators: the three reciprocal pairs XY/YX, XZ/ZX, and YZ/ZY remain rank deficient and generically leave a twofold ambiguity, whereas the remaining twelve pairs generically resolve the eightfold alias under explicit amplitude-nondegeneracy conditions. We then formulate a finite-shot adaptive reconstruction procedure that selects well-separated correlator groups and abstains near degeneracy, and we distinguish conditional reconstruction from held-out model auditing. The results concern identifiability within a restricted local-unitary model and do not constitute a new general tomography bound or evidence for additional physical states.

item.title: A Qubit No-Go Bound for Independent Commuting Finite-Order Controls
item.description: Two finite-order quantum controls may each be compatible with a qubit while their joint algebra is not. We study a cyclic control Q and an independent involution R with target algebra C_n x C_2. For even n >= 4, no faithful projective qubit realization exists: in PU(2) ≃ SO(3), a nontrivial involution commuting with an order-n rotation collapses to Q^(n/2). An explicit qutrit construction realizes the full algebra, so the minimum projective dimension is three; n = 4 is the first obstructed even member and has an eight-ray regular orbit. The representation-theory obstruction itself lies in a mature mathematical area. The operational contribution developed here is a calibrated qubit-consistency test: for exact quarter-turn and half-turn targets, the commutator angle gives a tight state-independent fidelity bound and a tight optimized binary-contrast cap. We derive a sufficient angular-error version and extend the test to general CPTP gate deviations through diamond distance. The explicit qutrit construction reaches the algebraic maximum binary contrast of one using two control sequences and a common binary measurement. The result is a calibrated falsification test for a qubit control model, not a device-independent dimension witness, and it remains entirely within standard finite-dimensional quantum mechanics.

item.title: Outcome-Frame Monodromy and Exact Limits of Marginal-Only Quantum Feedback
item.description: A quantum instrument is not determined by its induced positive-operator-valued measure (POVM) and nonselective channel, yet the global control consequences of this residual branch structure remain incompletely characterized. We study the nondegenerate fiber of instruments with both marginals fixed. The subgroup of outcome permutations preserving the effect tuple acts as the deck group of the ordered outcome-frame covering, and closed loops define a conjugacy-class-valued monodromy representation. Nontrivial monodromy obstructs continuous global branch labeling based only on local process continuity. We construct an explicit cyclic family with a uniform m-outcome POVM and a fixed completely dephasing channel, derive robust overlap-based reconstruction and a conservative finite-sample guarantee, and certify entangled conditional Choi states although the nonselective channel is entanglement breaking. For a noisy cyclic family, we prove an exact minimax separation in conditional feedback: recovery rules restricted to the two marginals and the reported local outcome have optimal worst-sector entanglement fidelity 1/m, whereas an outcome-frame-aware controller attains 1-lambda+lambda/m. The exact minimax value of the missing outcome-frame information is therefore (1-lambda)(1-1/m). The results remain entirely within standard finite-dimensional quantum mechanics and are positioned as an instrument-level, permutation-valued specialization of established Kraus-frame/channel holonomy with a distinct global-labeling and feedback limitation.

item.title: Temporal Correlations Reshape Causal Resources in Qubit Hamiltonian Recognition: Exact Two-Query General-Strategy Phase Diagram
item.description: Hamiltonian recognition asks which candidate Hamiltonian generated an unknown quantum evolution when the evolution angle is not observed. This preprint solves a binary two-query qubit setting in which the two unknown angles range from independently resampled to fully shared. A task-specific symmetrization theorem reduces the full sequential optimization exactly to a three-dimensional correlation elliptope. A nine-dimensional legal subset of the most general tester dual is then shown to reduce, by semidefinite-program duality, to the same elliptope problem, yielding P_GEN(beta,eta) = P_SEQ(beta,eta) throughout the stated parameter domain. The resulting PAR-versus-GEN phase diagram contains an exact interior equality curve and an exact high-angle reentrant regime in which the globally optimal causal-processing advantage vanishes at both zero and full temporal correlation but is positive at every intermediate strength. Arbitrarily weak temporal correlation can activate a strict advantage. In this archival v1.1 release, the weak-correlation statement is conservatively formulated as explicit constructive lower bounds of orders eta^2 below 45 degrees, eta^(4/3) at 45 degrees, and eta above 45 degrees. No matching upper-bound derivation is claimed for exact asymptotic equivalence of those exponents. The record includes the main preprint, Supplemental Material, and a reproducibility archive containing proof notes, symbolic verification scripts, numerical cross-check data, revised manuscript source, figures, and integrity hashes. Status: public preprint; not independently peer-reviewed.

item.title: Yuan–Eight–Binary Unified Physical Hypothesis: Master Experimental Validation Protocol v1\.0
item.description: This protocol converts the strong-form Yuan–Eight–Binary Unified Physical Hypothesis into a staged, falsification-first experimental validation program. The theory baseline is Zenodo DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22248366. The protocol separates four levels—Yuan pre-generative conditions, eight quantum/generative processes, hidden binary relational structure, and ordinary 0/1 observation—and defines E01–E11 experimental cards with explicit prerequisites, observables, PASS/FAIL rules, confound controls, and maximum permissible conclusions. It also introduces an S0–S6 evidence ladder so that a positive result at a lower layer cannot be used as proof of a higher layer. The protocol is platform-portable and is intended to be instantiated through device-specific preregistration annexes for quantum photonic, superconducting, trapped-ion/atomic, or other controllable quantum systems. The central unresolved quantitative task is the platform-specific bridge F(Ω,B,C)→G8, which must be frozen before the E10 bridge experiment is run.

item.title: From a Three-Condition Pre-Generative Structure to Eight Quantum Processes, Hidden Binary Structure, and Binary Observation: The Yuan-Eight-Binary Unified Physical Hypothesis
item.description: This preprint proposes a strong-form, falsifiable four-layer physical hypothesis in which ordinary binary outcomes are coarse-grained projections of deeper physical organization. The Yuan pre-generative layer consists of three jointly necessary conditions: a carrier/possibility domain, boundary and constraint conditions, and internal coupling/organizational relations. Their joint realization is hypothesized to generate eight physically distinguishable quantum process sectors. In the strong form, these sectors are organized as four relational directions and two orientations with a D4-type composition structure. The generative layer projects into a hidden-binary structural layer containing ordered complementary pairs 01/10, A/B/C/D source or directional labels, an independent orientation attribute, and a 3-to-6-to-96 fine-grained relational record space, before conventional measurement coarse-grains the structure to 0/1. The hypothesis is deliberately frozen before experimental validation. It predicts recoverable hidden information beneath identical binary outcomes, a minimal eight-process description, D4 noncommutative composition fingerprints, resolvable fine-grained relational records, necessity of the three Yuan conditions, and cross-platform consistency. The next stage is a preregistered experimental program designed to support, modify, or falsify each layer independently.

item.title: From Necessary Conditions to Binary Observation: A Working Hypothesis for a 3–8–2 Hierarchical Generative Framework
item.description: This paper proposes an exploratory “3–8–2” hierarchical generative framework designed to distinguish three different logical layers: a necessary-condition layer, a generative-process layer, and an observational-output layer. The current working hypothesis is: 3\ \text{necessary conditions} \rightarrow 8\ \text{candidate generative processes} \rightarrow 2\ \text{binary observational outcomes}. At the first layer, “Yuan” is provisionally defined as the minimal closed condition structure formed by three mutually irreducible and jointly necessary conditions. The number 3 therefore refers to the number of necessary conditions rather than to a number of physical states. At the second layer, the number 8 refers to eight candidate generative processes, process configurations, or generative pathways that may emerge once the necessary conditions are satisfied. Their precise mathematical origin and physical interpretation remain open. In particular, this framework does not assume that these eight processes correspond to an established eight-state quantum ontology. At the third layer, the number 2 refers to binary observational outcomes, represented as 0/1, obtained through coarse-graining, projection, or limited observational resolution. These binary outputs are therefore treated as observational results rather than as evidence that the underlying ontology is fundamentally binary. The aim of this work is not to claim a new physical ontology, but to formulate a testable hierarchical research framework that clearly separates the conditions required for a process to exist, the mechanisms through which structures or processes are generated, and the outcomes accessible to observation. The central open problem is to identify the three irreducible necessary conditions that constitute “Yuan” and to determine whether the minimum number of such conditions is genuinely three rather than two, four, or more. At its present stage, the proposed framework should be regarded as a working hypothesis and structural research program. Its possible connections to quantum processes, hidden structures, and physical realizations remain open and unproven.

item.title: Yuan (元), Primitive Distinction, and the Operational Descriptive Horizon: A Frozen Coarse-to-Fine Research Chain
item.description: This structural preprint freezes the current lower boundary reached in a continuing coarse-to-fine research program on observation, distinguishability, probability, admissible state spaces, dynamics, and finite readout. The paper introduces the provisional Chinese term Yuan (元) solely as a low-commitment placeholder for the presently unresolved side of the first expressible distinction. Yuan is not proposed as a state, object, field, observer, intrinsic capacity, or physical entity, and its existence is not asserted. The first layer that can currently be formalized is a relational distinction: a test, comparison, interaction, or reference yields at least two operationally different responses. From this layer the paper freezes a chain through primitive cut, event algebra, observer/test family, probability envelope, observer-resolution refinement, latent-state disclosure, relational/admissible state structure, dynamics/flow, projection/coarse-graining, and finite readout. The operational descriptive horizon is placed between Yuan and the first mathematically expressible relational distinction. Below that horizon, assigning a property to Yuan already reintroduces a distinction; above it, distinctions can be represented and tested. The horizon is therefore a limit of present descriptive resolution, not a claim that reality ends there. Quantum coherent superposition remains PARKED / UNMAPPED, and an observer-independent unique-actual-state hypothesis remains OPEN / UNPROVEN. The next phase is upward validation: refine observation or intervention and test whether a coarse equivalence class can be split into substructures with independently measurable responses. 中文描述 本文固化当前“由粗到细、再向更深层约化”研究所达到的暂时描述边界。论文暂时采用中文技术占位词 “元”,只用于标记“第一次可表达区分之前,目前仍无法被现有语言和数学无循环刻画的未知位置”。“元”不被预设为状态、对象、场、观察者、能力、物质、信息或任何已知物理实体,本文也不宣称“元”一定存在。当前第一个可以被数学化的层级是 关系性区分:某种测试、比较、相互作用或参照产生至少两个不同的操作响应。由此向上依次形成原始切分、事件代数、观察/测试族、概率包络、观察分辨率细化、隐态显化、关系/允许态结构、动力学/流、投影/粗粒化及有限读出。本文把 操作描述视界 放在“元”与“第一次可表达关系性区分”之间:视界以下,一旦试图给“元”赋予性质,就已经重新引入区分;视界以上,区分、事件、概率、状态和实验差异才开始能够被表示和检验。因此,该视界是当前描述分辨率的边界,不是存在的边界。量子相干叠加继续保持“暂缓 / 未映射”,观察者无关的唯一实际态假说继续保持“开放 / 未证实”。下一阶段转向向上验证:增加新的观察维度或干预,检验粗粒等价类能否裂分出具有独立可测响应的细结构。

item.title: Observer-Relative Undifferentiated Probability Envelopes: Operational Equivalence, Ontological Underdetermination, and the First-Distinction Boundary
item.description: This preprint introduces the concept of an observer-relative undifferentiated probability envelope(观察者相对的未分化概率包络) as a minimal operational description for situations in which a family of candidate underlying states cannot yet be distinguished by a specified observer, interface, or intervention set. Rather than treating “undifferentiated” as an absolute absence of structure, the framework defines it through an observer-induced equivalence relation on a candidate state space. When all candidate states belong to a single operational equivalence class, the observer has access only to a coarse probability-level description. The paper distinguishes two interpretations that must remain separate. Model A(模型A), adopted as the current operational description, treats the probability distribution itself as the minimal empirically justified state description. Model B(模型B) is retained as an open ontological hypothesis in which each individual realization may already possess a unique underlying actual state, while the observer has only incomplete knowledge of that state. Model B is neither accepted nor rejected; it is reserved for future tests that could produce predictions distinguishable from Model A. The analysis formalizes the first-distinction boundary using equivalence classes and partition refinement, shows that a minimal nontrivial refinement naturally produces two distinguishable classes without implying physical binary ontology, and emphasizes the distinction between operational indistinguishability and ontological identity. Quantum coherent superposition is deliberately not assumed as the deepest interpretation of the undifferentiated layer. Instead, quantum-state descriptions are treated provisionally as higher-level effective operational representations whose deeper interpretation remains open. This work freezes a temporary lower boundary in a broader research chain connecting observer-relative distinguishability, admissible state spaces, relational structure, dynamics, projection, coarse-graining, and finite observational readout. The next stage is to determine whether a deeper ontological completion can generate experimentally distinguishable consequences, or whether the probability-envelope description is operationally complete.

item.title: Pre-Projection Admissible State Spaces for Relational Rotation: A Structural Note on Flow, Coarse-Graining, and Finite Observational Readout
item.description: This structural preprint freezes an intermediate layer in a downward research decomposition. It separates an admissible pre-projection state structure, dynamical flow, observation/coarse-graining maps, and finite readouts. A planar relational-rotation benchmark shows that finite binary, eight-class, or twelve-sector readouts need not be identified with the dimension or ontology of the admissible state space. Common absolute orientation cancels from purely relational angle observables. The note explicitly does not claim a hidden-variable model, a new quantum state space, or a final ontology. It defines transition-relation reconstruction and discrete-versus-continuous symmetry as the next death gates.

item.title: Non-Abelian Information Loss under Homomorphic Binary Coarse-Graining of D4: Fourier Reconstruction, Symmetric Dynamics, and Coherent Reference Recovery
item.description: This preprint develops an exact mathematical and quantum-information framework for information loss under homomorphic binary coarse-graining of the eight-element dihedral group D4. It derives the D4→Z2×Z2 abelianization, an exact finite-group Fourier reconstruction using three one-dimensional character moments plus one 2×2 non-Abelian Fourier matrix, a two-rate symmetric D4 relaxation spectrum with the blind-prediction relation gamma_RS = gamma_R + gamma_S, an information budget for 8→4→3 coarse-graining and context-rich refinements, and a coherent-reference protocol in which the commutator residue -I is invisible as a target channel but observable as a relative phase. All results lie within standard probability theory, finite-group representation theory, and standard quantum mechanics; no beyond-standard quantum claim is made.

item.title: From Microscopic Complementary Closure to Macroscopic Binary Coarse-Graining: A Quantum–Binary Multilevel Observation and Dual-Projection Hypothesis
item.description: This work proposes a conceptual framework for connecting quantum closure structures, local observation, fine-grained binary records, and conventional binary coarse-graining. At the binary level, the framework introduces a structural representation distinct from ordinary ordered binary notation. The states 00, 11, and \{01,10\} are first grouped into three basic relational classes. Adding a positive/reverse distinction produces six states. Assigning one of four source labels, A, B, C, or D, to each of the two binary positions further generates 3\times2\times4\times4=96 labeled structural states. These 96 states are interpreted as a fine-grained record space rather than as 96 new conventional binary values. A separate quantum-level hypothesis is then introduced. In this candidate model, externally observed quantum values 0 and 1 are associated with complementary internal closure structures represented as 01 and 10. The labels A,B,C,D refer to four correlated positions or orientations within a single closed structure rather than to independent binary labels. Local observation of such a structure may yield source-labeled outcomes such as 0^A or 1^B. Repeated local observations generate source-labeled binary sequences, while conventional binary representation is obtained after discarding source, orientation, and positive/reverse information. The framework distinguishes microscopic structural complementarity from macroscopic statistical balance. A closed microscopic structure may be exactly complementary, while short binary observation sequences may still contain arbitrary local concentrations such as 0000 or 1111. Under symmetric and unbiased sampling conditions, long-run binary statistics may approach balance without requiring local balance at every observation step. The work also introduces a dual-projection viewpoint. The same underlying binary object can be represented through different observational rules. Conventional ordered observation yields the familiar four states 00,01,10,11, whereas relational observation yields the three classes 00, 11, and \{01,10\}, which may then be refined into the 3\rightarrow6\rightarrow96 hierarchy. These descriptions are treated as different coarse-grainings or projections of the same underlying object rather than as mutually exclusive binary systems. The 3\rightarrow6\rightarrow96 construction is presented here as a formally defined representational structure. By contrast, the proposed quantum 01/10 internal closure, the physical meaning of the A,B,C,D orientations, and any claimed quantum-to-binary correspondence remain hypotheses requiring mathematical formalization and experimental testing. Future work will focus on formal mathematical modeling, exhaustive state analysis, numerical simulation, comparison with standard quantum-mechanical predictions, falsifiable experimental protocols, and possible applications in quantum readout, feedback control, error diagnosis, and information processing. Version v0.1 is intended to establish a time-stamped record of the original hypothesis, definitions, conceptual boundaries, and research roadmap. It does not claim experimental confirmation of the proposed internal quantum structure.

item.title: A Falsifiable Closure Hypothesis Beneath Binary Quantum Readout: Two-Face Pairing, Eight Configurations, and Staged Experimental Protocols
item.description: This conservative preprint formalizes a candidate directional closure structure beneath ordinary binary quantum readout. A handwritten sixteen-face table is transcribed into eight complementary closure pairs: at each of four ordered slots, the paired faces preserve the direction label and complement the binary value. The accompanying inversion audit shows that a single value-plus-direction label, such as 0_A, does not uniquely reconstruct a closure pair; a second independent readout or a frozen dynamical rule is required. The paper proves the standard same-state indistinguishability boundary: if distinct preparation histories yield the same density operator and all subsequent operations are path-independent completely positive trace-preserving maps and POVM measurements, no path-dependent signal can occur. It then defines three staged experimental protocols and their conventional adversaries, including process memory, leakage, state-preparation-and-measurement error, and drift. This record is an openly testable hypothesis and experimental protocol. It does not claim observation of sub-quantum constituents, discovery of new quantum states, or a replacement for standard quantum mechanics. ```

item.title: DCR Open Validation Request: Three-Channel Cross-Intervention Model Separation
item.description: An open preregistration and reproducibility package for testing whether a constrained three-reservoir exchange model predicts a held-out recovery intervention better than registered standard competing models. The package contains the preregistered three-channel protocol, data dictionary, statistical analysis plan, competing-model definitions, reproducibility code, automated tests, and file-integrity checks. This package does not claim new particles, sub-quantum constituents, or physics beyond standard quantum theory. Its purpose is to enable an independent, falsifiable test of whether a mechanism-sensitive third observation channel improves cross-intervention model separation relative to registered standard alternatives.

item.title: A Qubit No-Go Bound for Independent Commuting Finite-Order Controls
item.description: Two finite-order controls can each be compatible with a qubit while their independent commuting joint algebra is not. For even n at least 4, C_n x C_2 has no faithful projective qubit realization but admits a qutrit realization. We derive a calibrated qubit-consistency tradeoff and a two-sequence binary test with maximal qutrit contrast. This is not a device-independent dimension witness and does not claim substructure below a qubit.

item.title: Fixed-Marginal Quantum Instruments and Hidden Feedback Frames
item.description: We construct equiprobable qubit instruments whose outcome probabilities and non-selective channel remain fixed while a hidden conditional feedback frame changes. The archive contains exact tight-frame and recovery results, a self-calibrated character-spectrum readout, verification code, and an unmitigated Rigetti endpoint benchmark. The benchmark is explicitly not treated as path-level monodromy or topology evidence.

item.title: Resource-Loss Spectroscopy of Hidden Quantum Symmetries: A Rational Resolution Limit and a Minimal Operational Remedy
item.description: We study reversible finite-group quantum instruments whose classical outcome record is coarse-grained over subgroups. The interactive-instrument resource loss is shown to equal a subgroup average of character intensity and to admit a direct Bell-return estimator. The resulting spectroscopy inherits a rational/cyclic-subgroup resolution limit. For a fixed labeled control oracle, two inequivalent three-dimensional representations of A5 are indistinguishable by every subgroup-resource measurement; they are exchanged by an outer automorphism, so the label-free gauge boundary is stated explicitly. A single class-sensitive five-cycle probe resolves the labeled ambiguity. A general rank-completion criterion identifies the minimum targeted probes needed to remove subgroup-incidence blind directions. The archive includes the manuscript, Supplemental Material, source files, code, frozen outputs, and finite-shot simulations. No hardware experiment is claimed.

item.title: Exponential Quantum Advantage in Clock-Free Generation of Recursive Temporal Words
item.description: This record provides the complete reproducibility and audit archive for the manuscript "Exponential Quantum Advantage in Clock-Free Generation of Recursive Temporal Words." It contains the manuscript, supplemental material, certified classical and quantum bounds, independent verification code, figures, numerical outputs, and integrity data. The result establishes a standard quantum-information separation for clock-free generation of recursive temporal words. It does not claim subquantum structure, QEM-8 confirmation, or experimental validation.

item.title: Exact Sign-Sector Probabilities for the Diagonal of a Haar-Random Rotation in SO(3)
item.description: Let R be a Haar-random rotation matrix in SO(3). We determine the exact probabilities of the eight sign sectors defined by the diagonal entries (R_{11},R_{22},R_{33}). Each sign sector containing an even number of negative diagonal entries has probability 5/24, while each sector containing an odd number of negative diagonal entries has probability 1/24. Consequently, the total probability of the four even-parity sectors is 5/6, and the total probability of the four odd-parity sectors is 1/6. Two independent analytic derivations are presented. The first uses the unit-quaternion representation of Haar-random rotations together with Hopf-coordinate integration. The second uses independent Gaussian squares and the associated Dirichlet distribution with parameters (1/2,1/2,1/2,1/2). High-precision numerical integration and Monte Carlo simulation are included as independent checks of the exact formulas. The structural description of rotation-matrix diagonals, the quaternion representation of SO(3), and the relevant Haar and Dirichlet distributions are classical. The contribution of this work is the explicit evaluation of the eight diagonal sign-sector probabilities. We did not locate these explicit values in the sources searched. item.title: A Forward Hypothesis of Recursive Closed Internal Structure Beneath Observable Binary States
item.description: 本文提出一种待验证的正向物理假设:外显二元状态0和1可能并非最终基本状态,而分别由方向相反的内部闭合关系01与10所生成。这里的01和10不被视为普通二进制字符串,而被视为具有顺序、方向、反演与闭合性质的不可约关系单元。 本文在暂时假定该假设成立的前提下,推导其可能产生的直接后果,包括同一外显状态下的内部差异、路径历史保留、内部反演、特征频率以及0/1镜像结构。进一步提出三种候选物理实现:方向—相位模型、概率流模型和闭合能量模型,并给出相应的正向实验验证路线,包括多路径相位实验、低功率弱谱学、内部反演搜索以及多类观测的联合检验。 本文不声称该假设已经获得实验确认,也不将三种候选模型视为最终物理结论。其目的在于把源于手稿的结构直觉转换为一个可计算、可证伪、可独立复现并可交由实验团队验证的研究框架,同时公开邀请具备量子控制、谱学、弱测量和多态读出能力的研究团队开展独立验证。 英文描述 This work proposes a falsifiable forward hypothesis that observable binary states 0 and 1 may not be fundamental, but may instead arise from oppositely oriented internal closed relations denoted as 01 and 10. These internal relations are not treated as ordinary binary strings, but as irreducible relational units carrying order, direction, inversion, and closure. Assuming the hypothesis is correct, the paper derives several possible consequences, including internal distinctions beneath the same observable state, path-history retention, internal inversion, characteristic frequencies, and mirrored structures between observable 0 and 1. Three candidate physical realizations are introduced: a directional-phase model, a probability-flow model, and a closure-energy model. Corresponding positive-direction experimental routes are proposed, including multipath phase tests, low-power spectroscopy, internal inversion searches, and joint analysis across multiple observables. No experimental confirmation is claimed, and the three models are not presented as final physical explanations. The purpose of this work is to convert a structural intuition originating from the author’s manuscript into a calculable, falsifiable, independently testable research framework, and to invite experimental teams with capabilities in quantum control, spectroscopy, weak measurement, and multilevel readout to conduct independent validation.

item.title: DCR-MRRS Hidden Risk Detector: A Three-Reservoir and Multiresolution Residual Framework for Early Risk Detection in AI Runtime Systems
item.description: This preprint proposes the DCR-MRRS Hidden Risk Detector, a strong engineering-hypothesis module for AI runtime safety. The method combines the DCR-8/6 three-reservoir redistribution model with the MRRS/RLM-2^n multiresolution residual spectrum. It decomposes runtime risk into three reservoirs: A_visible for explicit behavioral or safety-rule risk, H_hidden for latent drift and accumulated hidden residuals, and R_env for environmental or historical-record risk. Unlike conventional safety layers that mainly detect collisions, boundary violations, or triggered rules, DCR-MRRS aims to detect cases where the system remains visibly normal while internal trends continue to deteriorate. The paper describes the input schema, reservoir scoring formulas, the DCR_total aggregate score, the DCR_phase_score decision score, the Hidden Trend Gate, and four minimal simulated test groups. The paper-based simulation indicates that the method remains normal in the baseline group, identifies explicit danger via A_visible, detects hidden drift through H_hidden even when the conventional safety layer does not trigger, and separates environmental disturbance through R_env. This work does not claim real-system validation. It is presented as a validation-ready method proposal for the Replay, Shadow, and Advisory layers of AI18-DIOS.

item.title: Platform Integral as a Cross-System Mechanism for Window Formation in Hybrid Mode Systems
item.description:
Stable transmission or propagation windows are widely observed in hybrid mode systems, including polaritonic and photonic crystal structures. Conventional interpretations attribute these windows to local extrema, such as minimum residue or maximum group index. However, such pointwise descriptions do not fully explain variations in window width or consistency across systems.
In this work, we propose a platform integral framework for window formation. Instead of relying on local extrema, we introduce a global measure based on the structure of system-dependent landscapes:
P^* = \int \exp(-X/\langle X\rangle)\cdot \exp(-|\nabla X|/\langle|\nabla X|\rangle)\, d\Omega
where X represents a system-specific variable, such as residue Z_R in polariton systems or group velocity v_g in photonic crystal waveguides.
Across systems, a consistent principle emerges: local extrema determine the central position of the window, while the integrated weight of low-value plateaus governs the usable window width.
This framework is supported by data-driven results in polariton systems and is consistent with observations of flatband slow-light modes in photonic crystal waveguides.
These results suggest a cross-system structural mechanism for window formation based on platform integrals, providing a unified perspective beyond extremum-based interpretations.

item.title: Platform Integral Predicts Slow-Light Window Formation in Photonic Crystal Waveguides
item.description:
Slow-light phenomena in photonic crystal waveguides are commonly characterized by large group index values near band edges. However, the usable slow-light window is not solely determined by the peak group index.
In this work, we apply a platform integral framework to analyze slow-light window formation. Instead of relying on local extrema, we define a global measure based on the group velocity landscape:
P^*_{slow} = \int \exp(-v_g/\langle v_g\rangle)\cdot \exp(-|\partial_\lambda v_g|/\langle|\partial_\lambda v_g|\rangle)\, d\lambda
where v_g is the group velocity. Using published results on flatband slow-light modes in photonic crystal waveguides, we show that usable slow-light windows correspond to extended regions of low and slowly varying group velocity, rather than isolated extrema.
This leads to a structural interpretation: the peak group index determines the slow-light center, while the integrated weight of low-velocity plateaus governs the usable window width.
Together with prior polariton-based results, this supports a cross-system platform integral mechanism for window formation in hybrid mode systems.

item.title: Platform Integral Governs Stable Window Formation in Hybrid Modes
item.description:
Stable transmission or propagation windows are widely observed in hybrid mode systems, including polaritonic and photonic crystal structures. Conventional explanations attribute these windows to local extrema, such as minimum residue or maximum group index. However, such pointwise descriptions fail to account for variations in window width.
In this work, we introduce a platform integral framework based on the residue landscape Z_R(\theta). Instead of focusing on local minima, we define a global measure of low-residue and low-gradient regions:
P^*=\int \exp(-Z_R/\langle Z_R\rangle)\cdot \exp(-|\partial_\theta Z_R|/\langle|\partial_\theta Z_R|\rangle)\, d\theta
Using Hopfield coefficient data from polariton systems, we show that P^* correlates with stable window width and correctly predicts the ordering of observed configurations.
This leads to a structural conclusion: the minimum residue determines the mode center, while the integrated weight of low-residue plateaus governs the window width.
We further outline a mapping of this mechanism to slow-light photonic crystal systems, suggesting a platform-based description of window formation beyond local extremum models.

item.title: Protocol-Dependent Optimality in Near-Edge Systems: A Unified Explanation for Experimental Discrepancies in Slow-Light Regimes
item.description:
This work presents a unified framework for understanding optimal operating points in near-edge physical systems, with a focus on slow-light photonic crystal waveguides.
By introducing a Difference Explanation Model (DEM), we show that system performance can be described as a balance between enhancement (gain) and degradation (loss), where the latter is strongly influenced by experimental protocols such as coupling configuration, polarization, and mode selection.
The framework explains why similar structures can exhibit significantly different optimal operating points, and provides a predictive expression for the shift of the optimal point under different protocols. The model is supported by existing experimental observations in slow-light coupling and nonlinear enhancement systems.
This work aims to provide a minimal, testable criterion for analyzing near-edge systems, without replacing existing theories, but offering a higher-level explanation for experimental variability.

item.title: Structure-Aware Spectral Reconstruction via Observation Window Compensation
item.description: This work presents a structure-aware reconstruction framework for recovering suppressed high-order components under observation window distortion. In many imaging and signal acquisition systems, the observation process acts as a non-uniform filter that attenuates specific structural components, leading to incomplete or biased reconstruction. We model the observation process as a weighted projection over structural components and introduce a window compensation approach to invert such distortions. By estimating the observation window and applying component-wise correction, the proposed method enables recovery of hidden structural information that is otherwise inaccessible from single observations. Numerical simulations demonstrate significant improvements in reconstruction accuracy, robustness under noise, and tolerance to window estimation errors. The framework provides a general method for structure-level reconstruction in multi-component systems and can be extended to imaging, signal processing, and related applications.

item.title: A Structural Generative Control Framework: Behavior Mode Generation under Structural Constraints
item.description: This work proposes a Structural Generative Control Framework (SGCF), a novel control paradigm in which control is formulated as behavior generation under structural constraints rather than direct action computation. Unlike traditional approaches such as PID, MPC, and reinforcement learning, which map system states directly to control actions, SGCF introduces an intermediate behavioral layer defined by a finite set of behavior modes. These modes emerge as stable solutions of an underlying structure composed of driving forces, relational constraints, and system limitations. The framework demonstrates clear advantages in critical scenarios including goal–obstacle conflicts, instability, and rapid behavior switching. In these cases, SGCF maintains system feasibility through continuous transitions between behavior modes, avoiding discontinuities and collapse observed in conventional methods. SGCF provides a unified formulation bridging structure, behavior, and control, and establishes a new perspective for organizing control systems beyond optimization- and rule-based approaches.

item.title: SCBG Guardian: A Structure-Constrained Runtime Safety Layer for Behavior Stabilization
item.description:
We introduce SCBG Guardian, a runtime safety layer for dynamical systems that stabilizes behavior through structure-constrained mode selection.
Unlike conventional safety mechanisms based on threshold-triggered rules or constraint enforcement, SCBG Guardian operates by monitoring system states and dynamically switching between behavioral modes such as approach, avoidance, and stabilization.
The key idea is that safety is not enforced through fixed constraints, but emerges from transitions between structurally valid behavior modes defined by role-semantic invariants.
We evaluate SCBG Guardian in a minimal simulation environment and compare it against: (1) a nominal controller and (2) a threshold-based safety mechanism.
The results show that:
the nominal controller may achieve task objectives but fails due to collisions or instability, threshold-based methods avoid collisions but often lead to stalled or overly conservative behavior, SCBG Guardian avoids collisions while maintaining task progression through dynamic mode transitions.
These findings suggest that behavioral safety can be reframed as a structure-driven mode selection problem, rather than a constraint enforcement problem.

item.title: From Structure to Behavior: Role-Semantic Invariants as the Basis of Behavioral Mode Generation
item.description:
We propose a theoretical framework for behavior generation in dynamical systems, termed Structure-Constrained Behavior Generation (SCBG).
Unlike conventional approaches in control and learning, where behavior is derived from optimization or learned policies, SCBG suggests that behavior emerges as a constrained selection process defined by structural invariants.
A key contribution of this work is the introduction of role-semantic structural invariants, which extend traditional graph-based representations by incorporating functional roles associated with nodes and pathways. Within this framework, behavior is determined not by raw connectivity or parameter values, but by invariant structural relations including opposition, closure, hierarchical pathways, and role semantics.
Through a minimal experimental evidence chain, we show that:
structural differences induce distinct behavioral modes, perturbations of structural invariants lead to behavioral degradation, structural influence dominates input mapping, and behavior equivalence is preserved only under role-consistent structural transformations within a bounded scaling regime.
These results support a shift from policy-driven behavior generation toward structure-driven mode selection, suggesting a new perspective for understanding behavior in dynamical systems, robotics, and control.

item.title: Structure-Constrained Behavior Generation: Minimal Evidence for Structure-Dominant Behavioral Dynamics
item.description:
We propose a minimal framework for behavior generation in dynamical systems, termed Structure-Constrained Behavior Generation (SCBG).
Unlike traditional control paradigms where behavior is derived from optimization or learned policies, SCBG suggests that behavior emerges as a selection from a structure-constrained set of reachable modes.
We construct a minimal 2D agent model with fixed local update rules and compare multiple structural configurations. Experimental results show that behavioral outcomes, success rates, and stability metrics are strongly dependent on structural configuration, even under identical update rules and inputs.
Further perturbation studies indicate that structural modifications lead to significantly larger behavioral degradation than perturbations in input mappings, suggesting that structure acts as a primary determinant of behavior generation, while input plays a secondary, modulating role.
This work presents a minimal evidence chain supporting the hypothesis that behavior can be generated through structural constraints rather than direct policy optimization.

item.title: Defect–Fiber Spectral Geometry and Cosmological Freeze-Out: A Unified Framework for Higgs, Flavor, and Neutrino Structure

Within this construction, Higgs physics, flavor organization, neutrino suppression, and cosmological phase evolution are treated as different manifestations of a single defect-supported spectral geometry. Although not yet a complete fundamental theory, the framework defines a constrained and testable route toward a unified geometric organization of Higgs, flavor, neutrino, and cosmological freeze-out physics.

item.title: A Unified Low-Mode Field Framework for Critical Mode Mixing and Family Structure
item.description:
This work proposes a unified low-mode field framework describing critical mode mixing, slow-mode formation, and family structure generation across different physical systems.
The theory is formulated using a mother field defined on an extended manifold with an internal compact geometry. Through eigenmode decomposition and low-mode truncation, the dynamics reduce to an effective two-mode interaction structure characterized by parameters (A,B,C,Γ). with the boundary δ² + c² = 1 corresponding to slow-mode formation. Numerical scans reveal a universal phase diagram describing weak mixing, hybridization, and slow-mode regions.
The theory also provides a structural explanation for the emergence of three family states through internal eigenmode windows. The framework applies to multiple physical systems including photonic crystals, phonon dispersions, magnon hybridization, and quantum level mixing.
This work provides a unified structural language for critical mode mixing phenomena and suggests a cross-system theoretical framework for studying critical dynamics.

item.title: Core Compression Map for Collective Excitation Systems
item.description:

This work introduces a structural framework called the Core Compression Map, designed to compare collective excitation phenomena across different physical systems.
Many systems approaching dispersion boundaries exhibit similar structural behaviors, including reduced group velocity, dispersion flattening, and hybrid mode formation. The proposed framework represents these systems within a common phase diagram defined by the coordinates

The Core Compression Map provides a structural representation that may help compare collective excitation phenomena across photonic, phononic, and polaritonic systems.

This work serves as the methodological backbone of the QEM-Closure Series.

item.title: QEM-10: Control Theory and Testable Signatures of Non-Local Feedback in Quantum Entanglement Systems
item.description:
Abstract. We develop a control-theoretic framework of quantum entanglement built on an Oppositional Closure Network (OCN). When a local closure cannot be satisfied, the system performs an Instant Group Flip (I-GFlip) between the only two valid closures of a four-point unit (AB|CD and AD|BC) with no intermediate state. Under the Closure-Consistency Rule (CCR)—a shared edge that would break closure must flip—the flip cascades across an Entangled Square Lattice (ESL) as a Flip-Wave (FW). The framework preserves standard quantum-mechanical statistics and is compatible with no-signaling.
Contributions. (1) A unified structural model: OCN + I-GFlip + CCR + FW on ESL. (2) Six testable signatures (S1–S6) of non-local feedback and structural re-closure. (3) A closed-loop control law that suppresses instability (e.g., reduces CHSH-variance). (4) Two prototype routes: Silicon Photonic PoC-α and a pre-synchronization pulse for quantum gates.
Testable signatures (S1–S6).
S1 Gain cap: visibility/correlation vs. gain shows a hump; low-frequency self-excitation appears near the peak. S2 Distance plateau: fidelity/CHSH vs. distance exhibits a near-flat window [L_\downarrow, L_\uparrow] with sharp decay outside. S3 Threshold knee N^*: a knee and mild hysteresis when sweeping injected noise. S4 Micro-asymmetry boost: tiny inter-layer phase mismatch (≈0.5°–3°) increases stability before degrading. S5 Texture-lock sublinearity: phase-noise transfer becomes sublinear in textured/topological waveguides. S6 Invisible routing: keep total path length fixed; reshape peaks by only changing arm weights (center fixed, shape tunable).
Control law (discrete, summary). Let y_t be a target observable (e.g., CHSH S or visibility) and D_t the closure-debt (count of non-closing shared edges). The controller updates a phase/gain command u_t via u_t = k_p e_t + k_d(e_t - e_{t-1}) - k_c D_t, steering the network toward CCR-satisfying configurations and reducing instability.
Reproducibility. This record includes:
QEM-10_Manuscript.pdf (main paper); QEM-10_Supplement_Code.txt (minimal ESL toy model pseudocode for I-GFlip + CCR + FW); Suggested parameters: O/B/T triggers (0/1), defect density p, steps T, gain g, delay \tau, distance L, noise power N. Block-swap maps (AB|CD ↔ AD|BC), FW front shapes, and closure-debt trajectories can be reproduced from the toy model.
Clarification (no-signaling). Here “instantaneous” means a binary structural re-closure (I-GFlip), not energy or information transmission; the framework respects the no-signaling principle.
Keywords. Quantum Entanglement Mechanics; Oppositional Closure Network; Instant Group Flip (I-GFlip); Closure-Consistency Rule (CCR); Flip-Wave (FW); Entangled Square Lattice (ESL); No-signaling

item.title: QEM-9: Hyperstacked Mirror Lattices under the Opposition Principle (v2.1)
item.description:
English We extend the Quantum Entanglement Mechanics (QEM) framework from 3D mirror lattices to d-dimensional hyperstacked lattices governed by a Σ/Δ opposition principle. Transport and stabilization are computed in the odd (Δ) sector, yielding sector-resolved propagation bounds, stability-island delay limits, and a coherence scaling \xi_d \approx \xi_1/\sqrt{d} when \sum c_k^2 is bounded. We also summarize a design-for-opposition SOP for scalable architectures (bipartite layout, loop-parity constraints, and π-inverters on odd-Σ paths). QEM-8: Unified Equations for Hierarchical Mirror Lattices
item.description: Abstract (EN): We unify QEM-4–7 into a single field framework for hierarchical mirror lattices. Starting from a variational functional for Σ/Δ modes with a domain-wall order parameter, we derive coarse-grained equations across layers, an RG-like flow for effective couplings, and a universal causal-cone bound that collapses to QEM-5 locally and to an array form in QEM-7. The coherence length scales as ξ ~ |θ−θc|^{-1/2} at each level. We provide falsifiable predictions and cross-level protocols. Series note: This work is part of the Quantum Entanglement Mechanics (QEM) series by Youfu Wang (2025). 中文摘要 (ZH): 我们把 QEM-4–7 统一到层级镜像格的场论框架中:从变分泛函出发得到跨层粗粒化方程与“类重整化”的耦合流;统一的因果锥上限在局域退化为 QEM-5,在阵列退化为 QEM-7。相关长度在各层满足 ξ ~ |θ−θc|^{-1/2};重整后的参数把约束向上层级传递,给出芯片级时序预算、扇出与稳定窗口。并给出跨层可检验流程与普适性指纹(π 回声、sech² 包络、前沿速度塌缩律)。

item.title: QEM-7: Energy-Field Coupling and Feedback in Mirror-Flip Arrays
item.description: Abstract (EN): We extend the QEM-6 Mirror-Flip Unit (MFU) to device arrays and introduce an energy-field coupling model with readout–feedback control. Linearization around stationary domain-wall textures yields a Laplacian-spectrum-governed stability condition; we derive conservative bounds for feedback gain and delay, and generalize the flip-wave propagation limit to arrays. Three falsifiable protocols are provided: energy-flux pump–probe, feedback stability-island mapping, and array response spectroscopy. The results set timing budget, fan-out limits and safe operating windows for chip-oriented, controllable entanglement networks. Series note: This work is part of the Quantum Entanglement Mechanics (QEM) series by Youfu Wang (2025). 中文摘要 (ZH): 我们把 QEM-6 的最小镜像翻转单元(MFU)推广为阵列系统,提出带读出-反馈闭环的能量场耦合模型。在畴壁稳态附近进行线性化,得到由阵列拉普拉斯谱主导的稳定条件;导出反馈增益与延迟的保守临界,并将翻转波传播上限推广到阵列场景。提出三类可验证流程:能量通量泵浦-探测、反馈稳定岛扫描、阵列响应谱测量。结果为芯片级可控纠缠网络给出时序预算、扇出限制与安全工作区。系列说明:本作属于王有福(Youfu Wang)在 2025 年提出的 QEM 系列研究。

item.title: QEM-6: Mirror-Flip Quantum Unit as the Minimal Structural Cell of Entanglement
item.description: Abstract (EN): We introduce the Mirror-Flip Unit (MFU) as the minimal structural cell that realizes and stabilizes multi-body entanglement within the QEM framework. The MFU is a dual-layer mirror lattice supporting Σ/Δ collective modes with a controllable Δ-domain-wall profile that confines coherence. We derive governing equations near stationary textures, obtain the scaling ξ ~ |θ−θc|^{-1/2}, and predict falsifiable signatures: π-echo, sech^2 standing envelopes, and a causal front bounded by v_max ≈ (J ξ)/ħ. Protocols are provided for wall-fit (ξ), front-tracking (v_max), and stability-window mapping. Series note: This work is part of the Quantum Entanglement Mechanics (QEM) series by Youfu Wang (2025). 中文摘要 (ZH): 本文在 QEM 框架下提出“镜像翻转单元(MFU)”作为多体纠缠的最小结构元。MFU 由支持 Σ/Δ 集体模的双层镜像格架构成,其 Δ-畴壁用于相干约束。我们在稳态纹理附近给出动力学方程,得到相关长度缩放律 ξ ~ |θ−θc|^{-1/2},并给出可验证指纹:π 回声、sech² 驻波包络、以及由 v_max ≈ (J ξ)/ħ 限定的因果前沿。文末附有实验流程:畴壁拟合 ξ、前沿追踪 v_max 与稳定窗口测量。系列说明:本作属于王有福(Youfu Wang)在 2025 年提出的 QEM 系列研究。

item.title: QEM-5: The Upper Propagation Limit of Flip-Wave and the Causal Structure of Entanglement
item.description: This work extends the Quantum Entanglement Mechanics (QEM) framework to explore the upper propagation limit of flip-waves within multi-body entanglement systems. We introduce a causal-cone model that defines the boundary of correlation spread and demonstrate that flip-wave coherence cannot propagate faster than the intrinsic coupling velocity of the phase lattice. This finding bridges the topology of entanglement, the structure of causal boundaries, and the limits of quantum-information transmission. Series note: This work is part of the Quantum Entanglement Mechanics (QEM) series by Youfu Wang (2025).

item.title: QEM-4: Topological Domain-Wall and Stationary Interference Texture in Multi-Body Entanglement
item.description: The QEM-4 paper extends the Quantum Entanglement Mechanics (QEM) framework by introducing the concept of topological domain-walls emerging from mirror-coupled entanglement layers. These domain-walls act as internal interfaces where sequential flip-waves form stationary interference textures, analogous to internal double-slit patterns within the entanglement lattice. Analytical φ⁴-type solutions and critical-layer scaling relations are derived, providing testable predictions in coupled-qubit, ion-chain, and optical-lattice systems.

item.title: QEM-8³: Hierarchical Mirror Lattice and Sequential Flip-Wave Dynamics in Multi-Body Entanglement
item.description: We present QEM-8³, a hierarchical mirror-lattice framework for multi-body quantum entanglement. Non-commutativity of measurement order and basis rotation jointly induce Sequential Trigger Flips (STF), whose propagation forms Flip-Waves across nested mirror layers. We derive a coupled flip-wave equation, identify a Critical Layer (mirror–basis resonance), define the symmetry group G_{8^3} and a topological invariant T_{8^3}, and predict quasi-time-crystalline spectral oscillations, time-reversal echoes, and critical entanglement peaks.

item.title: QEM-8^3: Entanglement Square Lattice and Flip-Wave Dynamics
item.description: This paper introduces QEM-8^3, a three-dimensional extension of the QEM-8 entanglement framework. The model treats each entangled pair (A↔B and C↔D) as both an individual binary relation and part of a larger lattice system. By stacking the eight directional entanglement modes along vertical, horizontal, and depth axes, the structure forms a stable entanglement square lattice. The transitions between AB|CD and AD|BC are explained through measurement sequence, basis switching, and stability reconfiguration. The result is a discrete algebraic lattice that preserves absolute duality and relational symmetry across multi-quantum entanglement systems.

item.title: QEM-8: A Direction-Based Collapse Algebra for Quantum Entanglement Modes
item.description: This paper proposes QEM-8, a discrete directional-mode algebra explaining eight asymmetric quantum collapse modes. The framework provides mathematical insight into direction-conditioned entanglement and hidden causal asymmetry in quantum communication.
